page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the t2d server family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The CPU allocation is fully dedicated, running at 1.0 thread per physical core. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the single-core CPU performance of the t2d-standard-8 in the top 25% tier, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2688.09. Multi-core CPU performance falls into the middle 50% average tier, scoring 21511.57 in stress-ng. Memory bandwidth benchmarks also show average tier performance, with read-only small block speeds of 996.35 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds of 51.75 GB/sec. Cryptographic and integer operations are supported by hardware flags including AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, and ADX, though AVX-512 extensions are absent.

This instance is configured for workloads requiring a balanced ratio of compute to memory without local storage requirements. Database operations, static web serving, and software compilation perform within the average tier, as demonstrated by a PassMark database score of 6859.59 and a static web serving throughput of 11.61 GB/sec. Small-scale language model inference is possible, with prompt processing speeds of 1110.74 tokens/second for a 135M model and 33.49 tokens/second for a 7B model. The lack of local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators limits its applicability for large-scale deep learning or high-I/O storage-heavy tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 x86_64 processor. With 8 physical cores and a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio, it delivers strong single-core CPU performance in the top 25% tier, while multi-core performance and memory bandwidth remain in the average middle 50% tier. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, making it reliant on network-attached storage. It is equipped with hardware-accelerated cryptography and integer instructions, such as AES and SHA_NI, but lacks AVX-512 support. This configuration is suitable for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations, where a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio is required without the need for local high-speed storage.
